a novel diffusive gradients in thin film (DGT) with binding gel of metal-organic framework-derived porous carbon material has been developed for the measurement of sulfonamides and fluoroquinolone antibiotics in water samples.

the development of DGT for the measurement of a group of antibiotics, which are important pollutants of concern in the environment, and the application of the DGT to environmental waters.
the development and validation of a new DGT device based on PCM for in-situ monitoring of antibiotics.
the development and application of a DGT with PCM binding gel for the determination of antibiotics in water.

the novel PCM-based DGT is an efficient tool for in-situ measurements of antibiotics in environmental samples.
the DGT with PCM-based binding gel can be a powerful tool for in-situ measurements of antibiotics in waters.
the DGT with the PCM-based binding gel is a promising tool for monitoring antibiotics in environmental waters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a novel DGT based on PCM binding gel for in situ measurement of antibiotics in the environment.
DGT is a powerful technique for the measurement of TWA concentrations of trace contaminants in waters.
the novel binding gel of PCM was successfully used in DGT for in-situ monitoring of antibiotics in water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DGT can be a promising tool for in-situ monitoring of antibiotics and other organic contaminants in waters.
MOF-derived porous material can be applied as the binding gel in DGT for the in-situ measurement and time-weighted average (TWA) concentration determination of antibiotics.
the PCM-based DGT can be used for in-situ and time-integrated measurement of antibiotics in various environmental waters, and it can be applied for other organic contaminants.
